  "schema_version": "evidence_intent_extraction_v1",

  "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
  "draft_intents": [
    {
      "draft_id": "D0001",
      "locator": "page 60",
      "start_segment_id": "S00002",
      "end_segment_id": "S00005",
      "actor": "Mexico",
      "action": "maintained a tight fiscal stance and operated under a balanced-budget rule",
      "mechanism": "the fiscal stance and rule contained the projected debt path",
      "outcome": "IMF staff assessed overall sovereign-stress risk as moderate, while projecting elevated debt and no debt stabilization by 2027; the rule could restrain investment and development expenditure and thereby create a long-run budget-composition problem",
      "dates": ["2023", "2027", "extended 10-year period"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "The assessment was prepared in 2022 and directly evaluates the contemporary fiscal framework, with projections beginning in 2023.",
      "limitations": "The debt-containment effect was projected rather than fully observed; more favorable conditions were required for debt to decline over the extended horizon.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0002",
      "locator": "page 61",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00011",
      "actor": "Mexico's fiscal reporting system",
      "action": "excluded state and local governments from debt coverage and did not consolidate debt across the federal government and non-financial public sector",
      "mechanism": "subnational governments were excluded because of limited debt-carrying capacity and the absence of a federal legal obligation to guarantee or assume their debt; aggregate reporting instead represented gross individual liabilities",
      "outcome": "the debt-sustainability assessment lacked state and local debt and had no known data on accounts payable",
      "dates": [],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff commentary",
      "period_fit": "Contemporary disclosure limitation documented in the 2022 assessment.",
      "limitations": "IMF staff assumed that relevant accounts-payable information was included in other assessment data despite not knowing of direct data.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0003",
      "locator": "page 62",
      "start_segment_id": "S00006",
      "end_segment_id": "S00008",
      "actor": "Mexico's government",
      "action": "pursued a debt-management strategy that increased the share of longer-maturity liabilities",
      "mechanism": "the maturity extension accompanied broadly stable projected currency shares, while recent pension reforms increased domestic pension funds' holdings of public debt",
      "outcome": "overall debt-to-GDP was projected to remain broadly constant, and the longer-maturity share was expected to rise through 2025 and then stabilize",
      "dates": ["projection period", "2025"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff commentary",
      "period_fit": "The 2022 report describes the incumbent government's strategy and near-term projections.",
      "limitations": "The maturity and debt-ratio outcomes were projections, not completed results.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0004",
      "locator": "page 63",
      "start_segment_id": "S00011",
      "end_segment_id": "S00014",
      "actor": "Mexico",
      "action": "maintained a prudent fiscal-policy stance and was projected to run primary budget surpluses after 2023",
      "mechanism": "the projected primary surpluses offset unfavorable debt dynamics caused by low trend growth and relatively high average public-debt interest rates",
      "outcome": "public debt-to-GDP was expected to decline in 2022, increase in 2023 as global and domestic growth slowed, and avoid additional medium-term pressure from automatic debt dynamics through the projected surpluses",
      "dates": ["2020", "2022", "2023", "medium term"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff commentary",
      "period_fit": "The passage evaluates actual 2022 conditions and projections from 2023 onward.",
      "limitations": "Debt reduction in 2022 was partly attributable to post-pandemic recovery and exchange-rate appreciation; the later surplus and debt effects were projected.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0005",
      "locator": "page 64",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00013",
      "actor": "Mexico's fiscal and debt-management authorities",
      "action": "planned fiscal adjustment and longer bond maturities",
      "mechanism": "maturity lengthening reflected debt-management objectives, while projected fiscal adjustment operated through growth effects broadly consistent with standard multiplier assumptions",
      "outcome": "the three-year debt and cyclically adjusted primary-balance adjustments exceeded the comparator-country median but remained well below Mexico's historical maximum; projected real growth initially exceeded and then converged to potential growth as the output gap closed",
      "dates": ["past five years", "next five years", "three-year adjustment", "end of projection period"],
      "quantities": [],
      "attribution": "IMF staff commentary",
      "period_fit": "The report's 2022 baseline covers recent history and the subsequent projection period.",
      "limitations": "Pandemic observations biased the historical contribution of GDP growth downward; spreads reflected elevated early-projection uncertainty; growth and adjustment effects were model-based projections.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0006",
      "locator": "page 65",
      "start_segment_id": "S00008",
      "end_segment_id": "S00013",
      "actor": "Mexico's public financing system",
      "action": "relied on banks and other domestic institutional investors as potential absorbers of additional government financing needs under stress",
      "mechanism": "the banking system and pension funds had capacity to purchase additional government financing",
      "outcome": "IMF staff assessed medium-term sovereign-stress risk as moderate; low-probability downside scenarios could substantially increase public debt, but the rise in gross financing needs was assessed as moderate and absorbable",
      "dates": ["2022–2027", "medium term"],
      "quantities": ["government assets represented approximately 27 percent of banks' assets"],
      "attribution": "IMF staff commentary and medium-term risk analysis",
      "period_fit": "The risk window explicitly includes 2022 and extends through 2027.",
      "limitations": "The conclusion concerns modeled stress scenarios; the initial government-asset share in bank assets lay outside the comparator interquartile range, and no customized debt-stress scenario was triggered.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0007",
      "locator": "page 66",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00006",
      "actor": "Mexico",
      "action": "entered 2022 with comparatively low external debt and a projected decline below its pre-pandemic level",
      "mechanism": "post-pandemic economic rebound, excess capacity, strong remittance inflows, and nominal GDP growth contributed to small current-account deficits and a lower external-debt ratio",
      "outcome": "gross external debt was projected to fall to about 32 percent of GDP by the end of 2022 from a pre-pandemic 37 percent and remain near 32 percent over the medium term",
      "dates": ["pre-pandemic period", "end-2022", "medium term"],
      "quantities": ["approximately 32 percent of GDP by end-2022", "37 percent of GDP before the pandemic", "approximately 32 percent of GDP over the medium term"],
      "attribution": "IMF external debt-sustainability analysis",
      "period_fit": "Directly covers the 2022 target period and provides a medium-term projection.",
      "limitations": "The decline was driven substantially by rebound conditions, remittances, and nominal GDP growth rather than attributed solely to government policy; medium-term stability was projected.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0008",
      "locator": "page 66",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00009",
      "actor": "Mexico",
      "action": "faced downside risks to its external-debt trajectory from weaker growth, domestic policy mistakes, tighter global financial conditions, and currency depreciation",
      "mechanism": "those shocks could increase external risk premia, weaken the peso, and raise capital-flow volatility",
      "outcome": "a 30 percent real-effective peso depreciation could raise external debt to about 46 percent of GDP",
      "dates": ["2022 assessment horizon"],
      "quantities": ["30 percent real-effective depreciation", "external debt of approximately 46 percent of GDP"],
      "attribution": "IMF external debt-sustainability analysis",
      "period_fit": "Contemporaneous 2022 risk analysis.",
      "limitations": "The quantified outcome is a hypothetical stress scenario, not an observed event.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0009",
      "locator": "page 66",
      "start_segment_id": "S00010",
      "end_segment_id": "S00013",
      "actor": "Mexico's government",
      "action": "practiced prudent debt management and maintained favorable maturity and currency structures for public external debt",
      "mechanism": "more than 90 percent of public external debt had residual maturity above one year and roughly 30 percent was peso-denominated",
      "outcome": "these structures mitigated public-sector rollover risk; private-sector hedges and a well-capitalized, liquid banking sector further reduced vulnerability to external shocks",
      "dates": ["2022 assessment"],
      "quantities": ["public-sector external debt was around two-thirds of Mexico's external debt", "more than 90 percent had residual maturity over one year", "about 30 percent of external public debt was peso-denominated"],
      "attribution": "IMF external debt-sustainability analysis",
      "period_fit": "Describes debt conditions and management in the 2022 target period.",
      "limitations": "Some mitigating conditions belonged to private firms and the banking sector rather than directly to the ruler; the passage evaluates resilience rather than an observed stress outcome.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0010",
      "locator": "page 67",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00008",
      "actor": "IMF staff",
      "action": "tested Mexico's external-debt path against interest-rate, growth, current-account, combined, and real-depreciation shocks",
      "mechanism": "individual scenarios applied permanent half-standard-deviation shocks; the combined scenario applied permanent quarter-standard-deviation shocks to real interest rates, growth, and the current account; the depreciation scenario applied a one-time 30 percent real depreciation",
      "outcome": "the stress tests projected higher external-debt ratios than the baseline under adverse conditions",
      "dates": ["2017–2027 projection charts", "five-year projection horizon for historical scenarios"],
      "quantities": ["one-half standard-deviation individual shocks", "one-quarter standard-deviation combined shocks", "one-time 30 percent real depreciation"],
      "attribution": "International Monetary Fund country-desk data and staff estimates",
      "period_fit": "The projections encompass 2022 and subsequent years.",
      "limitations": "These are modeled bound tests based partly on ten-year historical averages, not observed policy outcomes.",
      "polarity": "neutral",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10"]
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0011",
      "locator": "page 68",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00003",
      "actor": "Mexico",
      "action": "reduced external debt sharply after its pandemic-era increase, with the baseline projecting near-stability thereafter",
      "mechanism": "identified debt-creating flows were negative in 2021 and 2022, while the non-interest current account was in surplus under the table's sign convention",
      "outcome": "external debt rose to 42.6 percent of GDP in 2020, fell to 34.5 percent in 2021 and 32.0 percent in 2022, and was projected to edge up from 32.3 percent in 2023 to 33.4 percent in 2027",
      "dates": ["2020", "2021", "2022", "2023–2027"],
      "quantities": ["42.6 percent of GDP in 2020", "34.5 percent in 2021", "32.0 percent in 2022", "32.3 percent in 2023", "33.4 percent in 2027"],
      "attribution": "IMF external debt-sustainability framework",
      "period_fit": "Contains an actual 2022 estimate and projections through 2027.",
      "limitations": "The table does not attribute the full debt movement to ruler decisions; values after 2022 are projections.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.10"]
    }
  ],
